reason: Two follow-ups to #587. (1) A retried subagent start (harness vendor retry, provider step replay) now returns the child's real status through SubagentService.start_output on both paths instead of a hard-coded running; a start that never ran fails again. (2) Browser companion refusals left after #581/#586 are classified per docs/TOOL_FAILURE_CONTRACT.md: another project's browser and a closed/revoked session are unavailable_resource, the service's pre-dispatch refusals (stale tab, misplaced file or credential reference, out-of-scope page) are invalid_arguments or permission_denied before execution, and the post-capture screenshot refusals report no side effects. Selected: the new test_subagent_start_replay.py and the whole of test_browser_companion.py (new provider-loop, harness-gateway and broker tests; needs Chromium for its real-browser test), the subagent files whose start path changed (test_harness_provider_subagents.py, test_chat_subagents.py, test_subagent_refusal_categories.py, test_chat_subagent_lifecycle.py, test_subagent_delivery.py), test_assistant_browser_viewer.py for the companion service's operator routes, and the browser-gateway nodes in test_harnesses.py and the companion stream node in test_api.py.
exclusions: Full suites are not approved and are excluded. No UI, native Rust/Tauri or Playwright code changed and the UI does not read failure categories, so frontend, native and playwright are empty. The rest of test_harnesses.py and test_api.py is unaffected: only _gateway_subagent's start result and the companion broker changed, and the selected nodes cover the browser gateway paths. The companion service's operator routes keep answering ValueError as before (CompanionRequestRefused subclasses it); test_browser_security.py, test_browser_host.py and test_browserd.py cover browserd and assessments, which are unchanged.
